title: Death Valley's 700-Pound Rocks Move by Themselves

scenes.text: In Death Valley, 700-pound rocks slide across the ground by themselves.
They leave trails hundreds of feet long, and for decades nobody had ever seen one move.
In 2013, scientists finally watched it happen.
Rain floods the dry lake, it freezes into ice thinner than a pencil, then it breaks into panels.
A ten-mile-an-hour wind pushes the ice, and the ice pushes the rocks.
No magic. Just ice, wind, and mud.

description:
Rocks as heavy as 700 pounds slide across Death Valley's Racetrack Playa, leaving trails hundreds of feet long.
In 2013 researchers finally saw it: thin ice panels pushed by light wind carry the rocks across wet mud.
Would you have guessed that?
first_comment: Rocks moved over 200 feet in the study. Which mystery should we solve next?
